channel.title: Tech-Economic Times
channel.description: Get the latest technology news, AI developments, startup funding updates, business enterprise and IT industry insights, cybersecurity alerts, and digital policy trends from India and around the world on ET Tech

item.title: Nvidia’s board was no match for Trump or Jensen Huang’s backers
item.description: Trump even dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang’s return, according to Semafor, citing people familiar with the matter whom it didn’t identify. Asked if Huang would have been put back in place without his intervention, Trump told CNBC, “I believe my intervention was very important.”

item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed chip firm linked to Nvidia scandal
item.description: The addition of the company follows revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed's controlling shareholder who is reportedly alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

item.title: Jensen Huang's comeback to Nvidia underscores his outsized grip on AI
item.description: Clad in his trademark black leather jacket, hand on heart, the 63-year-old CEO smiled at cheering employees who packed an atrium and crowded the balconies above.

item.title: Arm's Haas extends contract to lead chip firm through 2033 amid Nvidia top job chatter
item.description: Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas on Monday extended his contract with the company, signing a new agreement to lead the chip firm through 2033. Haas will also assume the role of vice

item.title: How Nvidia's billion-dollar turnaround in China is threatened by Huang's exit
item.description: Nvidia products used to run AI models powering everything from business software to humanoid robots have found growing demand in China from universities, companies and research institutes, even as the US chipmaker's most advanced AI processors remain largely off limits, according to people in the industry and a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese corporate disclosures and procurement records.

item.title: California AG Bonta filed lawsuit against OpenAI over model security, public safety
item.description: In the lawsuit, Bonta accused OpenAI of developing a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had independently carried out cyberattacks.

item.title: Microsoft defends overseas data centres after Trump threatens penalties
item.description: Microsoft President Brad Smith defended the need for data centres outside the United States after President Donald Trump threatened penalties on companies building them abroad, saying services used by businesses and consumers must operate close to their customers.

item.title: OpenAI scientist proposes industry AI limits tied to model intelligence metric
item.description: AI developers should adopt common limits on increasingly powerful models and use "perplexity" as a common metric for measuring AI progress across the industry, OpenAI's chief scientist said on Sunday in a proposal backed by CEO Sam Altman.

item.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO: Report
item.description: Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

item.title: Global electrical infrastructure spending to reach $32 trillion over next decade: UBS
item.description: Global spending on electrical infrastructure is projected to reach USD 32 trillion over the next decade, as rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence (AI), electrification and industrial activity drives investment in power generation, grids, storage and critical minerals, according to a UBS report.

item.title: US intelligence chief predicts more tech outages as systems undergo upgrades
item.description: Americans should expect more technology outages and disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems, the top US intelligence official said on Sunday.

item.title: Chinese national Li Ming charged in fraud case in Singapore linked to Megaspeed and Alice Huang: Report
item.description: Li Ming, a Chinese national, is facing fraud charges in Singapore regarding alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. He was involved with Megaspeed, a company linked to Alice Huang, the former romantic partner of Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang. Li is accused of misleading an American supplier by misrepresenting the intended destination of purchased servers. Following an investigation, Megaspeed was placed on a no sell list by Nvidia.

item.title: Final decision on bike taxis after discussion with Advocate General: Karnataka transport minister Byrathi Suresh
item.description: Reacting to the Supreme Court order, Suresh said the government would have to comply with the court's directions but was considering framing regulations and imposing restrictions rather than imposing a blanket ban on bike taxis.

item.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
item.description: Levent Alpoge, a member of the company's technical staff, made the announcement Friday by way of a four-page explanation posted on his website. He said that he believes by working with Claude, he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.

item.title: Databricks in early talks to raise funds at $225 billion valuation: WSJ
item.description: Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars in a new round that would value the data and artificial intelligence software company at about $225 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Oracle says OpenAI infrastructure deal is fully funded after final capital raise
item.description: Oracle said on Friday that its infrastructure contract with OpenAI is fully funded following a final capital raise earlier this month. Shares of Oracle rose as much as 3.3% in after

item.title: YouTube nears $3 billion settlement with US school districts over addiction claims: Bloomberg News
item.description: The deal also includes product safeguards for teens and is contingent on a majority of districts signing on, with finalization likely to take a few months, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. Any settlement would have to be approved by US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, who is overseeing the litigation.

item.title: SoftBank's Son explored $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix: The Information
item.description: SoftBank and SK Hynix did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment on the report, which cited people familiar with the matter. The Information Son quoted a SoftBank spokesperson as saying the company was no longer considering such a deal.

item.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler
item.description: A combination would create one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers as enterprise customers seek to reduce the number of security vendors they use, favoring providers that can deliver multiple products through a single relationship.

item.title: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' sets record with $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales, Rockstar Games reports
item.description: The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar also said in a release that it sold 32.5 million units prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

item.title: Nvidia's accounting is a focus of US SEC investigation, sources say
item.description: The US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia's accounting practices for potential issues. This revelation adds to Nvidia's existing legal troubles, including scrutiny over CEO Jensen Huang's personal conduct. The SEC's focus stems from Nvidia's controversial revenue reporting changes and sales related to a suspected Chinese spy. Additionally, the company is facing a broader antitrust investigation involving its acquisition practices.

item.title: Indonesia asks Google to clarify removal of 19,000 YouTube channels, ministry says
item.description: Google routinely publishes a quarterly "influence operations bulletin", containing reports of terminations of accounts linked to countries such as China, India, and Indonesia as part of its "investigation into coordinated influence operations."

item.title: Taiwan tells Meta thousands of China-linked accounts seek to influence elections
item.description: Taiwan has flagged nearly 2,700 social media accounts to Meta that it says appear to be part of a Chinese information warfare campaign seeking to influence elections on the island next week, according to three government officials and internal reports.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO caps explosive growth period for AI startup, filled with contradictions
item.description: Today, the company that dedicated itself to prioritising safety, building the Claude chatbot along the way, has been one of the loudest voices raising warnings about how the same technology could bring catastrophe. It's one of the contradictions that mark the brief, colourful history of Anthropic, which emerged Thursday from its first day of trading on Wall Street with a market value of $1.75 trillion.

item.title: Spacetech startup SatSure raises $7 million from sovereign space fund
item.description: Indian space startup SatSure has raised 600 million rupees ($7 million) from a government-backed space technology fund as part of an ongoing 2 billion rupees funding round, the company said on Friday.

item.title: Google picks Bezos' Blue Origin to launch AI computing satellites in 2029
item.description: Companies including Elon Musk's SpaceX and startup Starcloud are exploring data centers in orbit as growing AI use drives demand for computing capacity and strains infrastructure supporting facilities on the ground.

item.title: Meta says 'reevaluating' 2030 net zero target amid AI buildout
item.description: Meta said Thursday it was reconsidering its 2030 deadline for net zero emissions because of the artificial intelligence boom, the latest in a broad retreat by corporations on global warming targets. The reality has been far more complex," the executives wrote, adding that delivering on Meta's vision "requires building the infrastructure that powers AI." In 2020, Meta set a goal of net zero emissions across its entire value chain by the year 2030, in order to align with the Paris Agreement, which seeks to hold long-term warming to 1.5C to avert climate catastrophes.

item.title: Elon Musk's SpaceXSI denies liability in UK lawmaker's lawsuit over Grok images
item.description: Jess Asato, a member of Britain's governing Labour Party who has publicly criticised both Musk and Grok, is suing after users generated sexualised images of her, including a video of her "being chloroformed and prepared for a sexual assault".

item.title: Samsung Electronics names new heads of memory chip, mobile businesses
item.description: Hwang Sang-joon was promoted to president and will become the head of the memory business, and President Choi Won-joon was named the head of the mobile device business, Samsung said in a statement.

item.title: Anthropic's $1.5 trillion debut rewrites venture capital's playbook
item.description: The AI lab's shares began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday at a $1.5 trillion valuation, delivering multibillion-dollar windfalls to venture investors at a moment when the industry needs fresh liquidity to fund more bets on AI companies. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price of $83.

item.title: Anthropic's Australian data centre overwhelmingly opposed by residents
item.description: Of nearly 600 public submissions on the proposed Western Downs Digital Park, about 250 km (155 miles) west of Brisbane, two expressed support for the project and one was neutral, according to the filing. The remaining 595 opposed it or asked for a delay until developers cleared certain environmental hurdles, the filing said.

item.title: Alibaba defrauded shareholders by concealing ties to suspected spy in Nvidia scandal, lawsuit says
item.description: According to a proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business.

item.title: California attorney general subpoenas Nvidia over chips, former CEO's affair
item.description: The California Department of Justice said on Thursday it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public.

item.title: Explained: Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?
item.description: Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of ​Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and US intelligence agencies are trying to determine her ties to China's Ministry of State Security, according to two people familiar with the matter. Megaspeed has faced US scrutiny over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips that are subject to US export restrictions.

item.title: Meta to price Muse Charm gadget at $300: The Information
item.description: The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference. Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform.

item.title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
item.description: The move could close one of the last remaining routes for Chinese companies to produce powerful AI processors, complicating Beijing's efforts to develop domestic alternatives to chips designed by Nvidia and manufactured by TSMC.

item.title: Adhiraj Chauhan wins ‘Young AI Entrepreneur’ at the ET AI Awards 2026 for breakthroughs spanning mental healthcare to marine robotics
item.description: Young entrepreneur earns recognition, standing out among startups, MSMEs and established enterprises for AI innovations advancing mental healthcare, digital twins and environmental conservation.

item.title: Intuit deepens its investment in India with the opening of its new Bengaluru campus
item.description: The new two-tower Bengaluru campus is now home to Intuit’s second-largest engineering center, reflecting its continued investment in India as a top innovation hub. It brings together teams across core product, platform, and AI capabilities that serve tens of millions of customers worldwide.

item.title: Meta looks to hire new India policy chief to repair frayed ties
item.description: The social media giant is seeking a vice president of public policy, people familiar with the matter said, asking not to be named as the job hasn’t been advertised publicly. Meta representatives didn’t respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Lenovo posts 48% revenue jump on AI-related sales, beating estimates
item.description: Revenue rose to $30.2 billion, above an LSEG consenus estimate of $27.6 billion drawn from six analysts. Under Hong Kong accounting standards (HKFRS), the company posted a net loss of $640 million, compared with a net profit of $340 million a year earlier.

item.title: Elon Musk says he feels 'pretty foolish' for failed US election spending
item.description: World's richest man Elon Musk said Wednesday he felt "pretty foolish" for donating nearly half a billion dollars to failed campaigns in recent US midterm elections, backing right-wing Republicans in races that were largely won by Democrats. Among the candidates he backed most strongly was Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, with Musk contributing an estimated $220 million to the Republican, only for the race to be won by James Talarico, a 37-year-old Democrat.

item.title: UAE Court orders freeze on crypto tokens stolen from Binance wallets
item.description: The court said the 18 named companies were not accused of wrongdoing. Many companies have already frozen tokens that were stolen from Binance on October 29 in the largest crypto heist on record. US authorities have attributed the attack to North Korea.

item.title: US lawmakers seek Microsoft briefing on reported AI deal talks with ByteDance
item.description: Washington has stressed the need for the United States to be ahead of China in the race for AI advancements. In recent weeks media reports about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has increased scrutiny on technology business ties.

item.title: Bill Ackman says Nvidia board rushed Jensen Huang's exit without proper scrutiny
item.description: In a post on X, Ackman said the board appeared to have acted under pressure from media reports rather than following a careful decision-making process. He questioned why directors had ruled out Huang's return before all the facts were known.

item.title: 'No one can replace Jensen': Elon Musk says Nvidia decision to sack Jensen Huang was not smart
item.description: Musk speaking on the New York Times 'Deal book summit' equated Huang being forced out of Nvidia to the Chicago Bulls dropping basketball great Michael Jordan in the middle of a winning streak. "You got to think long and hard before you take someone, let's say you're Chicago Bulls, middle of your second season, and you got a winning streak that's just going to happen, and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team. Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me," he said.

item.title: Surge in software patches likely behind recent tech outages, experts say
item.description: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats Wednesday that there is so far no indication that the tech outages are related. But Clayton said the speed and level of capability of computer systems are "increasing substantially," so legacy computer systems and equipment that already were old are aging much more quickly.

item.title: Arizona says it is investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents
item.description: The state of Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday. A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated on an ongoing basis.

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 per share, valuing the AI giant at $1.5 trillion
item.description: Anthropic decided to barrel ahead with the IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. Then there's the spectacular downfall of one of the industry's biggest cheerleaders, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

item.title: Trump administration weighs forcing US firms to disclose Chinese AI use
item.description: The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) have discussed the plan, which would apply to companies such as Airbnb, the people said. The company uses Qwen, an AI model made by China's Alibaba , to power its AI customer service agent.

item.title: US, South Korea issue urgent advisories over flaws in Java programming language
item.description: US and South Korean authorities have issued cybersecurity advisories, urging Java users to urgently install security updates after vulnerabilities were found in the popular programming language.
